name: The Meat We Chose: A Philosophy of Elective Embodiment
creator: Dr. Priya Okonkwo-Saarinen
description: A dense, rigorous philosophical text arguing that the post-augmentation human body is the first genuinely self-authored form of consciousness in evolutionary history — and that this represents a moral obligation, not merely a freedom. Okonkwo-Saarinen, a former neural ethics professor expelled from Meridian Polytechnic for undisclosed reasons, draws on phenomenology, West African philosophy of personhood, and Finnish existentialist traditions to construct her argument. It is demanding reading, nearly 600 pages, and has no neural-optimized abridgment — she refuses to authorize one.
medium: physical hardcover (premium print run of 2,000); unauthorized neural text scan circulates widely
cultural_impact: Became the foundational text of the Elective Embodiment movement and is cited as philosophical justification by both extreme augmentation communities and, controversially, by some geneware modification advocates seeking legal personhood protections.
controversy: Okonkwo-Saarinen's argument has been weaponized by Tier 4-5 corporate bioethicists to argue that unaugmented Tier 1 residents have 'failed their moral obligation to self-author' — a reading she has publicly and furiously denounced. The unauthorized neural scan is missing a critical chapter.
story_hooks: The missing chapter in the pirated neural scan contains an argument so politically explosive that someone paid to have it excised — finding the original file could destabilize a major biotech corponation's legal standing.
Okonkwo-Saarinen has gone into hiding and left a message for someone the player character knows, asking them to deliver the only surviving manuscript of her follow-up work.
A Tier 1 community has adopted a radical misreading of the text as their philosophical charter — and their interpretation is leading them somewhere dangerous.
